question.text: Can a company undertake a buyback of shares with the objective of delisting its shares from a stock exchange?

answer.text: Yes, if it obtains prior SEBI approval
Yes, if it follows the delisting regulations simultaneously
Yes, but only through the tender offer method
No, buyback cannot be used as a mechanism to delist shares

explanation.text: The Logic: A company shall not buy back its shares or specified securities so as to delist them from the stock exchange (NISM-Series-IX workbook, p.221). Page 44 reinforces this by stating that no company shall apply for, and no stock exchange shall permit, delisting pursuant to a buy-back of equity shares. The Trap: SEBI approval, parallel delisting procedures, or restricting the route to tender offers do not unlock a delisting-by-buyback option; the prohibition on pp.44 and 221 is direct. Note: Anchor on the buyback-cannot-delist rule from pp.44 and 221 rather than reasoning from procedural alternatives.
